subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-097.draft.md
summary: D-097 is tightly limited to the five D-096 candidates, keeps mechanics and owner-recording separate, and produces no readiness or implementation effect. Its core authority source nevertheless fails: a coordinator-composed draft under review cannot turn old general completion instructions into the new express condition-2 role grant required by D-096 (A). D-054 records the controlling precedent that this form cannot widen delegation and that the remedy is a user-made amendment. The current review dispatch requests review but does not itself grant the listed roles. The claimed verbatim record is also abbreviated and ellipsized. In addition, the overturn path omits reconciliation of the separate dependent MF-6 notes that the draft says will follow later owner-recordings. One MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX remain, so CONSENT is forbidden.

objections.title: No direct user act supplies the express condition-2 owner grant
objections.finding: The subject is a coordinator-composed DRAFT being submitted to D-000 review, yet lines 33-65 make the operative preference-laden grant on the user's behalf. Lines 25-29 merely reuse three earlier general completion/delegation statements; they do not contain a direct user statement expressly granting the newly enumerated condition-2 candidate roles. Reviewer consensus can assess the boundary of a grant already made, but it cannot create user intent or widen delegation. Calling this the same class as D-054 does not cure the defect because D-054's adopted artifact says the opposite: its amendment was made directly by the user, and the prior coordinator-composed grant was objected because that form cannot widen delegation. The current user dispatch asks Codex to review frozen D-097 bytes; it does not say that the user grants or adopts D-096 (A).
evidence: D-096 lines 51-60 require an applicable owner grant that expressly covers every named role for the candidate being recorded; mechanics alone never grants.
D-097 lines 7-11 describe a preference-laden user amendment, lines 25-29 quote only old general completion messages, and lines 33-65 perform the new exact-role grant inside the reviewed draft.
D-054 user-amendment lines 3-8 state that the adopted amendment was made directly by the user and that C2-D054-01 rejected a coordinator-composed grant because that form cannot widen delegation.

D-054 lines 22-31 map the reused completion instruction to condition-1 V1 Route-B owner roles. D-097 expressly refuses to invoke D-054/D-057 for the new condition-2 rows, so those adopted acts do not supply D-096 (A).

The heading 'User words, recorded verbatim' is inaccurate: D-097 item 3 replaces most of D-054's full item 4 with an ellipsis, and item 1 is also an abbreviated excerpt rather than an exact newly issued role grant.
objections.impact: If adopted, D-097 would make reviewer approval the source of a preference-laden authority expansion. Later owner-recordings could cite it even though the user never directly and expressly granted the listed condition-2 roles, violating D-096's prerequisite and the D-054 authority precedent. Because supplying grant (A) is this subject's sole operative purpose, the defect is fatal to adoption.
objections.requiredRepair: Obtain a new direct user message that either (a) expressly authorizes the assistant to perform preview-scope owner-recordings for exactly the D-096 candidates and roles listed here as grant (A), while excluding mechanics, SATISFIED, file 08, implementation, and all other roles, or (b) explicitly adopts the exact grant section of a pinned draft as the user's own decision. Record those exact new user words without abbreviation or invented expansion, then freeze and review a new subject. The independent reviews may verify transcription and scope but must not be treated as the act that grants authority.

objections.title: Revocation omits reconciliation of dependent MF-6 effects
objections.finding: Lines 90-92 establish that a later owner-recording will be followed by a separate MF-6, but lines 94-98 say overturn requires only C-D097 and supersession of owner-recordings that used it. Once an MF-6 has relied on such an owner-recording to mutate file 08, superseding the owner record alone does not reconcile that separate readiness act. D-057's established reversibility model explicitly requires reconciliation of every dependent MF-6 note under its own reviewed act.
evidence: D-097 lines 90-92 make the separate MF-6 part of the contemplated downstream effect chain.
D-097 lines 94-98 mention dependent owner-recording supersession but omit the dependent MF-6 note.

D-057 turn-3 lines 118-121 distinguish revoking authority/mechanics from undoing effects and require both superseding each owner-recording and reconciling each dependent MF-6 note under its own reviewed act.
objections.impact: A revoked grant could leave file 08 carrying a disposition whose authority chain has been superseded, creating stale readiness evidence and an incomplete rollback procedure.
objections.requiredRepair: State that revocation stops future uses, and that undoing prior effects requires both superseding every owner-recording that cites D-097 and reconciling every dependent MF-6 note under a separate reviewed act. Do not imply that C-D097 itself edits file 08 or automatically overturns those later acts.
